svg.text: Storage Architecture
CipherVault Physical File & Database Storage Layout
Complete storage topology: 4 authoritative filesystem directories vs. MySQL 8.0 relational metadata segregation
Physical Server Storage Hierarchy (storage/)
1. storage/encrypted/ (Authenticated Ciphertext Blobs)
• Contents: Physical file blobs encrypted via streaming AES-256-GCM.
• File Naming: UUID format: {uuid}.ext (e.g. 58d9008f-1e6e-4aad-b30f-09cd306699b8.pdf).
• Binary Structure: [ 12-Byte Nonce ] + [ Ciphertext Chunks ] + [ 16-Byte GHASH Tag ].
✔ Zero plaintext on disk. Protected at rest. Cryptographically unreadable without user UDEK.
2. storage/uploads/ (Unencrypted Upload Staging)
• Contents: Files uploaded when user explicitly disables the encryption toggle switch.
• File Naming: UUID format: {uuid}.ext (retains original format for direct streaming).
✔ Accommodates public non-sensitive documents where encryption overhead is unnecessary.
3. storage/previews/ (Thumbnail Cache)
• Contents: Downsampled JPEG preview thumbnails generated by MediaPreviewService.
• File Naming: preview-{uuid}.jpg (served via GET /api/files/{id}/preview).
✔ Allows instant mobile grid rendering without decrypting heavy multi-gigabyte payloads.
4. storage/profile_photos/ (User Avatars)
• Contents: Custom user account profile images uploaded from Android Settings.
• File Naming: photo-{uuid}.jpg (served via GET /api/user/photo).
✔ Linked to users.profile_photo_path; synchronized across all active sessions.
✔ Directory Initialization
All 4 directories are initialized automatically on Spring Boot bootstrap via FileStorageConfig.java.
Path traversal attacks are blocked via strict FileStorageConfig.resolvePath() containment checks.
Relational Metadata Segregation (MySQL 8.0)
Crucial Architectural Invariant: ZERO Binary Bytes in DB
• MySQL stores zero file binary content bytes (no BLOBs or large text encodings).
• Stores structured relational metadata, filenames, quotas, hashes, and disk path pointers.
• Preserves extreme database query speed, microsecond latency, and small SQL backup sizes.
✔ Entire test database backup is only ~548 KB, despite containing gigabytes of stored vault data.
Decoupled Relational Schema Scope
• users: User identity, password hashes, PBKDF2 wrapped UDEKs, token_version, and 10 GB quota.
• stored_files: Original filenames, stored filenames, sizes, content types, and SHA-256 digests.
• file_metadata: 29 decoupled forensic EXIF attributes (optics, resolution, codecs, author).
• activity_events: Immutable security audit trail recording login, upload, download, and delete.
• transfers: Real-time streaming throughput, batch identifiers, byte counters, and statuses.
✔ Cryptographic Deduplication Constraint:
UNIQUE (user_id, sha256_hash) enforces atomic per-user deduplication without side channels.
✔ Cascading Lifecycle Consistency
• When a file is deleted via DELETE /api/files/{id}:
1. Relational database cascades delete to file_metadata via foreign key ON DELETE CASCADE.
2. users.used_storage quota is decremented atomically by the exact file size.
3. Server unlinks the physical ciphertext blob from storage/encrypted/.
4. Server unlinks the cached thumbnail from storage/previews/.
✔ Guarantees 100% synchronization between database records and physical disk files.
All 4 storage directories and MySQL database tables verified directly from FileStorageConfig.java and database/schema.sql.
